title: solute uptake
intro: The ’solute uptake’ component calculates uptake of nitrogen through roots.

sections.name: diffusion
sections.desc:
N is transported to the root surface based on diffusion and convection.
   The convection is based on concentration in the soil, while the diffusion is based
on concentration in both soil and at root surfaces.
   This base model find variables ’A’ and ’B’, so the transport of nitrogen to the
root surface is calculated as A - B * CRoot, where CRoot is the concentration at
the root surface. See also [Hansen and Abrahamsen, 2009]

Log Variables
    alpha: number (dimensionless) soil cells
     Internal variable.
    A: number (dimensionless) soil cells
     CRoot independent N uptake.
    B : number (dimensionless) soil cells
     CRoot dependent N uptake factor.
    D: number [cm2 /h] soil cells
     Diffusion variable.
    beta: number (dimensionless) soil cells
     Internal variable.

sections.name: fixed sink
sections.desc:
A ‘diffusion’ model (see 81.1, page 443) build into Daisy.
   Find the highest value of ’CRoot’ that meets the N demand. See also [Hansen and Abrahamsen, 2009]

A ‘diffusion’ model (see 81.1, page 443) build into Daisy.
   Find the highest value of ’CRoot’ that meets the N demand. See also [Hansen and Abrahamsen, 2009]

    CRoot: number [g N/cm3 ]

sections.name: variable sink
sections.desc:
A ‘diffusion’ model (see 81.1, page 443) build into Daisy.
   Nitrogen uptake limited by the root ability to assimilate N.
   The transport of N to the root surface is given as
   A-BC
   The assimilation of N from root surface is given as
   F1 C / (K1 + C) + F2 C / (K2 + C)
   We find the C for which
   A - B C = F1 C / (K1 + C) + F2 C / (K2 + C)
   If this is higher than the demand, uptake is scaled down. See also [Tsay et al., 2007,
Miller and Cramer, 2005]

attrs.name: K1
attrs.doc:
Value description: 50 uM See also [Tsay et al., 2007]
        K parameter for high affinity uptake.

attrs.name: K2
attrs.doc:
Value description: 5 mM See also [Tsay et al., 2007]
        K parameter for low affinity uptake.

attrs.name: F relative
attrs.doc: Fraction of max uptake accounted for by high affinity uptake.

attrs.name: C1
attrs.doc:
CRoot calculated assuming C >> K1. Solution to A - B C = F1 + F2 C /
        (K2 + C).

attrs.name: C2
attrs.doc:
CRoot calculated assuming C << K2. Solution to A - B C = F1 C / (K1 +
        C) + F2 C / K2.

A ‘diffusion’ model (see 81.1, page 443) build into Daisy.
   Nitrogen uptake limited by the root ability to assimilate N.
   The transport of N to the root surface is given as
   A-BC
   The assimilation of N from root surface is given as
   F1 C / (K1 + C) + F2 C / (K2 + C)
   We find the C for which
   A - B C = F1 C / (K1 + C) + F2 C / (K2 + C)
   If this is higher than the demand, uptake is scaled down. See also [Tsay et al., 2007,
Miller and Cramer, 2005]
  < variable sink (K1 7e-07 [g N/cm3 ])
                          (K2 7e-05 [g N/cm3 ])
                          (F relative 0.1 [<fraction>]) >

       K1 : number [g N/cm3 ]
        Parameter (default 7e-07)
        Value description: 50 uM See also [Tsay et al., 2007]
        K parameter for high affinity uptake.

       K2 : number [g N/cm3 ]
        Parameter (default 7e-05)
        Value description: 5 mM See also [Tsay et al., 2007]
        K parameter for low affinity uptake.
       F relative: number [<fraction>]
        Parameter (default 0.1)
        Fraction of max uptake accounted for by high affinity uptake.

Log Variables
       CRoot: number [g N/cm3 ] soil cells
        Nitrogen concentration at root surface.
       C1 : number [g N/cm3 ] soil cells
        CRoot calculated assuming C >> K1. Solution to A - B C = F1 + F2 C /
        (K2 + C).

       C2 : number [g N/cm3 ] soil cells
        CRoot calculated assuming C << K2. Solution to A - B C = F1 C / (K1 +
        C) + F2 C / K2.
       CEst: number [g N/cm3 ] soil cells
        Best of C1 or C2..
